entry.title: Presenting at IEEE/CVF WACV 2025
entry.content:
I had the incredible opportunity to present our latest research, “CT-to-PET Translation: A Large-scale Dataset and Domain-Knowledge-Guided Diffusion Approach”, at the IEEE/CVF WACV2025 conference. This experience was both an honor and an exciting moment to share our findings with the computer vision communities.

Our work was selected for an oral presentation, which allowed me to introduce our novel approach to a broad audience. I also participated in a poster session, engaging in discussions with researchers from diverse backgrounds. These interactions provided valuable insights and new perspectives on improving our methodology further.

Networking & Discussions: Conference is not just about research but also about making new connections.

WACV 2025 was an enriching experience, and I am excited to apply the feedback and ideas from discussions into future research. Stay tuned for upcoming publications and collaborations!

entry.title: Presenting at ACM Multimedia Asia 2024
entry.content:
I had the incredible opportunity to present my latest research at ACM Multimedia Asia 2024, held from December 3–6, 2024, in Auckland, New Zealand. The conference brought together researchers and practitioners from the multimedia community to share cutting-edge advancements and insights.

During the conference, I presented my paper titled “Action Selection Learning for Multi-label Multi-view Action Recognition”. My research focuses on enhancing action recognition models by leveraging multi-view perspectives and multi-label learning techniques to improve accuracy and robustness in real-world scenarios.

A huge thank you to my co-authors, advisors, and the conference organizers for making this event a success. I truly appreciate the opportunity to contribute to the multimedia research community.

entry.title: Master’s Graduation from Nagoya University 🎓
entry.content:
I am thrilled to announce that I have successfully completed my Master’s degree at Nagoya University, Japan! It is an immense honor to have been recognized as the Honorary Valedictorian of the Graduate School of Informatics.

My journey through the Master’s program was filled with challenges, discoveries, and personal growth. Through rigorous research, collaborative projects, and insightful mentorship, I have gained invaluable knowledge in the field of Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia Information Processing.


Gratitude & Acknowledgments

This achievement would not have been possible without the unwavering support and guidance of my esteemed professors, Professor Ichiro Ide, Professor Takahiro Komamizu, and Professor Yasutomo Kawanishi.

I am deeply grateful for their mentorship, encouragement, and invaluable insights throughout my academic journey. Their guidance has shaped my research mindset and technical expertise, and I look forward to continuing this collaboration in the next phase of my studies.

Next Chapter: PhD Journey Begins!

As one chapter closes, another begins! I am excited to share that I will be continuing my academic journey as a PhD student at Nagoya University. My passion for AI, action recognition, and multimedia research drives me forward, and I look forward to contributing innovative solutions to this ever-evolving field.

entry.title: Presenting at IEEE FG 2024
entry.content:
I had the honor of attending the IEEE International Conference on Automatic Face and Gesture Recognition (FG 2024) to present my research on “One-Stage Open-Vocabulary Temporal Action Detection Leveraging Temporal Multi-scale and Action Label Features.” The conference was an amazing experience, filled with insightful discussions, exciting presentations, and great networking opportunities.

In my talk, I introduced a novel one-stage open-vocabulary approach for temporal action detection, which leverages both multi-scale temporal features and action label embeddings. This method aims to improve action recognition in real-world, open-vocabulary settings, addressing the challenge of detecting actions beyond predefined categories.

A Special Thanks to Professor Mugan

One of the most memorable parts of this trip was meeting Professor Mugan, who kindly arranged our pick-up and drop-off at the airport. His generosity and warm hospitality made our experience in Istanbul even more special.

It was a pleasure meeting you, Professor Mugan! Thank you for your kindness and for making our trip smoother.
